doc.title: Frank Wess interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Majesty of the Seas, May 29, 1995

title: Recording engineers and sound men
summary: Engineers should listen to the band in the room before recording.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: It would be much better if the recording engineers would come out in the room and hear the music they’re trying to record before they listen over those speakers, you know. Because most of them don’t have the slightest idea of what they’re recording. You know all they hear is what comes over that speaker. They don’t ever come out in the room and listen to the band, to really hear what’s going on. And so I’d like to get them out there too. They’ve got to see that.
And move away from their knobs.
Yeah. That’s their security blanket. But actually it’s really gotten—and you know if you’re going to make an authentic reproduction of something, you have to know what you’re trying to reproduce.
Know what the real thing sounds like.
Before you try to work with what the mechanized thing sounds like.
But that’s our business, so we have to suffer that a lot of times.
